argument: The pause must live in loop geometry: release after a measured interval needs to change the addressed loop's opening and rotation, then carry a real lag into later loop positions. A timer label or glow cannot substitute for changed coordinates.

With labels, readout, controls, captions, and furniture hidden, the first field should read as one sparse procession of separate suspended loops with an interval, not a node lattice, membrane, tile wall, or decorative ring diagram. After a pause, the opened loop and downstream delay must be findable in the silhouettes.

Arming and a short tap must remain non-causal. Only a real hold and release above 420ms, the deterministic measure control, Enter, or Space may commit; Delete restores the exact prior procession and R releases bounded memory.

v024 must leave the lattice, adaptive field, and continuous membrane through a separate-loop composition, a duration-bearing hold-and-release encounter, and a memory model in which delay propagates downstream instead of opening a surface or rerouting cells.

Delete v024 if the loops are only a decorative ring chart, if duration does not affect geometry, if a tap commits, if later loops ignore the stored lag, if exact lifting fails, or if the caption is needed to understand that the archive keeps an interval.
